articles.title: Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy: Rajat Patidar sets record for most sixes with an unbeaten 135 off 48 balls
articles.summary: Rajat Patidar, who recently withdrew from India's Rising Stars Asia Cup squad in Doha to manage existing injuries, has made his priorities clear: T20
articles.body: Rajat Patidar, who recently withdrew from India's Rising Stars Asia Cup squad in Doha to manage existing injuries, has made his priorities clear: T20 cricket is where his focus lies.On Monday, the Madhya Pradesh and Royal Challengers Bengaluru captain produced a record-breaking Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy innings, smashing an unbeaten 135 off 48 balls against Assam in New Chandigarh.His knock, studded with 13 sixes and eight fours, powered MP to 250 for six before Assam were bowled out for 119 in 17.4 overs, giving MP a 131-run win. Patidar's 13 sixes are the most by any batter in a single SMAT innings. He also became the first Madhya Pradesh player to score a century in the tournament's history, reaching the landmark in just 41 balls. "It was an outstanding knock. The beauty of Rajat's innings was that he was hitting the ball where he wanted to," MP coach Chandrakant Pandit told TOI.Surya continues red-hot runSuryakumar Yadav continued his stunning return to form, following his 21-ball 60 against Hyderabad with 82 off 29 balls as Mumbai beat Gujarat by eight wickets at the Jadavpur University Campus Ground in Kolkata.Chasing 198, Mumbai got home in 15.4 overs. Suryakumar hit nine fours and seven sixes, bringing up his fifty in 18 balls before falling to Ravi Bishnoi in the 11th over. Mumbai had earlier bowled Gujarat out for 197 in 19.2 overs, with Shardul Thakur taking three for 30 in 3.2 overs on return from a finger injury. Mumbai slipped to 25 for two in the chase before Suryakumar added 86 off 39 balls with Hardik Tamore.Mayank stars in Delhi's winMayank Yadav also extended his fine run, taking four for 12 in three overs to set up Delhi's 109-run win over Punjab.After Yash Dhull's unbeaten 78 off 40 balls helped Delhi post a comfortable 240 for five, Mayank followed up his five for 14 in the previous match by helping bowl Punjab out for 131 in 17.5 overs.At the Wankhede Stadium, Uttar Pradesh beat Karnataka by 16 runs. UP made 204 for five and restricted Karnataka to 188 for nine despite Ravichandran Smaran's 68 off 39 balls.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Selector jahan baitha hai, wahin maarna hai': MS Dhoni movie inspires Suryakumar Yadav's India comeback bid
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India T20I batter Suryakumar Yadav is determined to return to the national team and is making his presence felt in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India T20I batter Suryakumar Yadav is determined to return to the national team and is making his presence felt in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2026.The Mumbai captain has scored two consecutive half-centuries in the tournament, showing signs of a return to form. After losing his place in the Indian T20I team earlier this year, Suryakumar is looking to catch the attention of the BCCI selectors with consistent performances.He scored an unbeaten 60 off just 21 balls against Hyderabad in Mumbai's tournament opener on November 14. He followed it up with an even bigger knock against Gujarat on Monday, smashing 82 off 29 balls.Suryakumar recalls MS Dhoni movie dialogueAfter his explosive innings against Hyderabad, Suryakumar spoke about his approach and revealed that his focus was on scoring runs consistently and helping Mumbai win matches.He also recalled a famous dialogue from the film 'M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story' while explaining his mindset."You must have watched the movie 'M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story' where Mahi bhai's friend had said, 'Selector jahan baitha hai, wahin maarna.' My plan was also the same today. I'm trying to score runs as consistently as possible, help win matches, and play the 'high-risk, high-reward' game at Nos. 3 to 5," Suryakumar told reporters.Shiv Sundar Das, a member of the BCCI Senior Men's Selection Committee representing the East Zone, was also present at the ground. A few IPL scouts were also watching the match as Suryakumar attacked the Hyderabad bowlers.One of his sixes even went beyond the Jadavpur University 2nd Ground in Salt Lake.'Entertainment wala format hai, khul ke khelo ekdum'Suryakumar made it clear that he was not trying to send any special message to the selectors. He simply wanted to enjoy his batting and play the way he always had."It's not about making any statement or anything; I just want to enjoy the way I've always played. Entertainment wala format hai, khul ke khelo ekdum," stated Suryakumar.He also spoke about the six he enjoyed hitting straight down the ground and explained how his practice was helping him execute such shots in matches."I enjoyed watching the six I hit straight down the ground. But I have been practising it a lot. And if you execute on the ground what you've done in practice, that means your practice is successful," he added.Suryakumar smashes second successive fiftySuryakumar continued his impressive run on Monday, smashing 82 off 29 balls against Gujarat in Mumbai's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy match.Mumbai chased down Gujarat's target of 198 in just 15.4 overs. Suryakumar's innings included seven sixes and nine fours, while Sarfaraz Khan provided support with an unbeaten 40 off 17 balls.Gujarat had posted 197, thanks to late contributions from Ashutosh Sharma (42 off 22 balls) and Vishal Jayswal (38 off 21 balls).Shardul Thakur and Atharva Ankolekar picked up three wickets each for Mumbai.Suryakumar had earlier scored an unbeaten 60 off 21 balls against Hyderabad on November 14. The two consecutive half-centuries have given him a strong start to his campaign as he looks to fight his way back into the Indian team.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IPL 2027 Retention Live Updates: Travis Head, Mitchell Starc, Trent Boult released; MS Dhoni retires from IPL
articles.summary: IPL 2027 Retention Live Updates: With the IPL 2027 mini-auction approaching, all 10 franchises have the option of keeping their entire existing squad
articles.body: IPL 2027 Retention: Punjab Kings release Lockie Ferguson, Nehal Wadhera and four others Punjab Kings have released six players ahead of the IPL auction, with New Zealand fast bowler Lockie Ferguson and Indian batter Nehal Wadhera among the notable names to be let go. Mitch Owen, Pyla Avinash, Praveen Dubey and Vishal Nishad are the other players released by the franchise. The departures free up Rs 10.1 crore in Punjab Kings' purse..IPL 2027 Retention: SRH release Travis Head, Gerald Coetzee and seven others Sunrisers Hyderabad have released nine players ahead of the IPL auction, with star Australian opener Travis Head and South African pacer Gerald Coetzee among the notable names on the list. Kamindu Mendis, Jaydev Unadkat, Dilshan Madushanka, Onkar Tarmale, Amit Kumar, Shivam Mavi and David Payne are the other players released by the franchise. The releases free up Rs 21.35 crore in SRH's purse.IPL 2027 Retention: CSK release Matthew Short, Matt Henry and eight others Chennai Super Kings have released 10 players ahead of the IPL auction, with Matthew Short, Matt Henry and Zak Foulkes among those let go by the franchise. Prashant Veer, Aman Khan, Kuldip Yadav, Akash Madhwal, Dian Forrester and Macneil Noronha are the other players released. MS Dhoni also features on the list following his retirement from the IPL, with the former CSK captain set to take up a mentor role with the franchise. The releases free up Rs 24.5 crore in CSK's purse, giving the five-time champions additional flexibility as they prepare for the auction..IPL 2027 Retention: Mumbai Indians release Trent Boult, Deepak Chahar and seven others Mumbai Indians have released nine players ahead of the IPL auction, with big names such as Trent Boult and Deepak Chahar featuring on the list. AM Ghazanfar, Atharva Ankolekar, Keshav Maharaj, Mohammed Izhar, Danish Malewar, Mayank Markande and Mayank Rawat are the other players released by the franchise. The move frees up Rs 28.8 crore in MI's purse..IPL 2027 Retention: KKR release 11 players ahead of IPL auction Kolkata Knight Riders have made a major reshuffle ahead of the IPL auction, parting ways with several players, including Akash Deep, Blessing Muzarabani, Matheesha Pathirana, Mustafizur Rahman, Navdeep Saini, Rachin Ravindra, Rahul Tripathi and Umran Malik. Daksh Kamra, Luvnith Sisodia and Tejasvi Singh are also among those released, while Ajinkya Rahane has retired..IPL 2027 Retention: Gujarat Titans release Ishant Sharma, Mark Wood, Shahrukh Khan and two others Gujarat Titans have released five players ahead of the IPL auction, including Ishant Sharma, Mark Wood, Kulwant Khejroliya, Shahrukh Khan and Connor Esterhuizen. GT's pace resources remain well stocked, making the decision to part ways with Ishant and Khejroliya relatively unsurprising. Ishant did not feature in a single game, while Khejroliya got only a handful of opportunities. The release of Shahrukh Khan, however, suggests the franchise may have finally run out of patience with the all-rounder..IPL 2027 Retention: RCB release Jacob Bethell, four others ahead of IPL auction RCB have released Jacob Bethell, Richard Gleeson, Mangesh Yadav, Satwik Deswal and Vihaan Malhotra. Bethell's release comes as a surprise given the franchise's high regard for the England all-rounder. However, with an Ashes year ahead and England's focus on Test preparations, his likely limited availability during the IPL season may have influenced the decision. .IPL 2027 Retention: Travis Head, Mitchell Starc, Trent Boult released Big names on the move! Travis Head, Mitchell Starc and Trent Boult among the high-profile players released ahead of the IPL auction. .IPL 2027 Retention: “You’ll always be our Thala, our captain”- CSK captain Ruturaj Gaikwad thanks MS Dhoni Chennai Super Kings (CSK) captain Ruturaj Gaikwad on Tuesday paid tribute to former skipper MS Dhoni, recalling the lessons he learnt from the legendary cricketer and expressing gratitude for sharing the dressing room and field with him. In an Instagram post, Gaikwad, who took over the CSK captaincy reins from Dhoni ahead of the 2024 season, described simplicity as the biggest lesson he learnt from the legendary cricketer after joining the franchise in 2019. He said observing Dhoni closely, despite his numerous achievements, taught him the true meaning of the word. “Simplicity,” wrote Gaikwad in his Instagram post, before adding, "I got to learn the exact meaning of this word when I first joined CSK in 2019 by watching you through the lens as much as possible, that was the biggest lesson I learned despite of all the achievements that you have accumulated over the years! To share the dressing room ,the field,the 22 yards and to finish games with you is what are dreams made of. You are and You Will always Be OUR THAALAA, our captain and our Leader! Thank you Mahi bhai for everything." .IPL 2027 Retention: Harshal Patel traded to Gujarat Titans from Sunrisers Hyderabad Seam bowler Harshal Patel was on Tuesday traded to Gujarat Titans (GT) from Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) for Rs 4 crore ahead of next year's Indian Premier League (IPL) season. The 35-year-old Harshal was bought by SRH for Rs 8 crore in the 2025 mega auction. Known for his variations and tactical nous, the wily pacer brings considerable experience, having played 124 matches and claimed 151 wickets across four franchises since making his IPL debut in 2012. A consistent performer over the years, the seasoned campaigner was the leading wicket-taker in the 2021 and 2024 editions of the tournament, representing Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) and Punjab Kings (PBKS) respectively. He had a productive first season with SRH, taking 16 wickets in 13 matches at an economy rate of 9.80 in IPL 2025. However, his opportunities dried up in IPL 2026 as the franchise preferred uncapped Indian pacers Praful Hinge and Sakib Hussain. Harshal featured in just five matches in IPL 2026 and went wicket-less, conceding 10.82 runs per over. .IPL 2027 Retention: Mohammed Shami to join Rajasthan Royals, traded from Lucknow Super Giants Veteran India pacer Mohammed Shami will play for Rajasthan Royals in the Indian Premier League 2027 season after he was traded from Lucknow Super Giants on Tuesday. Shami, who recently retired from Test cricket, will move to RR for Rs 8 crore. He was traded to LSG from Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) last year for Rs 10 crore. The 36-year-old Shami will further strengthen RR’s bowling attack with his tremendous skillset and striking ability. The right-arm pacer has 145 wickets from 132 IPL matches so far. Meanwhile, left-arm spinner M Siddharth, known for his accuracy and control, will also move to RR from LSG for his existing fee of Rs 75 lakh. England all-rounder Sam Curran has also been traded to LSG from RR for his existing fee of Rs 2.4 crore. He has claimed 59 wickets and scored 997 runs in his IPL career so far. .IPL 2027 Retention: MS Dhoni’s IPL legacy- Five titles, 5,439 runs and several records Former Chennai Super Kings captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni may have brought the curtains down on his playing career in the Indian Premier League, but the numbers he leaves behind tells the story of one of the most influential figures in the tournament's history. From leading Chennai to five titles to setting remarkable wicketkeeping and captaincy records, Dhoni's contribution to the league extends far beyond his batting numbers. With the former India captain now stepping away from playing duties and preparing to take up the role of CSK’s team mentor from IPL 2027, let's have a look at his record-breaking stats in the tournament. Dhoni finished his IPL career with 278 matches and 5,439 runs at an average of 38.30 and a strike rate of 137.45. His tally includes 24 half-centuries, 264 sixes and a highest score of 84 not out. Despite playing predominantly as a middle-order batter and often taking responsibility for finishing games, he never scored an IPL century. His leadership record remains among the most impressive in the competition. Dhoni captained teams in 235 IPL matches, the highest by any player, and registered 136 victories. His association with Chennai produced five championship triumphs in 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023, putting him alongside Rohit Sharma as the most successful captains in terms of IPL titles. The Ranchi-born cricketer also guided CSK to 10 final appearances, making the franchise a regular contender for the championship during his tenure. He led the side through different phases of its journey, including its return to the competition in 2018 following a two-year suspension. His contribution was not restricted to leadership and batting. Dhoni finished with 205 dismissals as a wicketkeeper, comprising 158 catches and 47 stumpings, the highest combined tally in the tournament. His sharp glove work and ability to effect stumpings in a fraction of a second became defining features of his game. Another notable aspect of his batting was his flexibility. Dhoni produced half-centuries from five different positions in the batting order, demonstrating his ability to adjust according to the demands of an innings. He also holds the distinction of hitting 218 sixes while captaining IPL teams, underlining his ability to combine leadership responsibilities with attacking batting. Dhoni’s association with CSK began in the inaugural IPL season in 2008. Over the years, he became closely identified with the franchise, with his finishing ability, calm approach and leadership helping shape its identity. His playing career may have concluded, but his connection with Chennai will continue as he moves into a mentoring role ahead of the 2027 season. .IPL 2027 Retention: 'There is no CSK without MS Dhoni'- N Srinivasan's emotional message, calls signing Thala in 2008 his 'best decision' Mahendra Singh Dhoni will take on the role of mentor for Chennai Super Kings starting in the 2027 IPL season. The franchise expressed their intention to keep Dhoni involved, even after his retirement from playing. Owner N Srinivasan lauded his invaluable contributions, while co-owner Rupa Gurunath pointed out that his vast experience will be pivotal in guiding the younger players. .IPL 2027 Retention: Mohd Shami, M Siddharth move to Rajasthan Royals; Sam Curran joins Lucknow Super Giants in trade deal Rajasthan Royals and Lucknow Super Giants have completed a player trade ahead of the IPL 2027 season. Mohd Shami and M Siddharth are joining Rajasthan, while Sam Curran moves to Lucknow. Shami brings extensive IPL experience after playing with Lucknow Super Giants previously. Siddharth, a left-arm spinner, adds depth to Rajasthan's bowling options for the upcoming season. Curran's all-round abilities will enhance Lucknow's capabilities in both batting and bowling departments. .IPL 2027 Retention: MS Dhoni's IPL legacy Mahendra Singh Dhoni's playing career in the IPL ended on Tuesday after he was appointed the mentor of his franchise Chennai Super Kings. The writing was on the wall for 45-year-old whose participation as a player in the franchise had reduced over the years due to recurring injuries. The statement issued by CSK did not have any comment from the superstar wicketkeeper-batter. "There is no CSK without MS Dhoni. For nearly two decades, we have walked and grown alongside each other, through triumphs, setbacks and everything in between," said CSK owner N Srinivasan in the statement. "MS will continue to be a part of the CSK family as a mentor. His experience and expertise are invaluable to us, especially during this phase of transition. With many youngsters in the squad, his guidance will help shape the next generation of CSK," added Rupa Gurunath, Srinivasan's daughter and co-owner of the franchise. The World Cup-winning captain had retired from international cricket in August 2020. Dhoni led CSK to five IPL titles, was their second-highest scorer with 5,314 runs, and most-capped player with 272 appearances. .IPL 2027 Retention: MS Dhoni moves into mentor's role after IPL retirement .IPL 2027 Retention: MS Dhoni calls time on IPL career MS Dhoni moves into a new role at Chennai Super Kings! The legendary former captain takes charge as team mentor after retiring from the IPL, with the move set to free up Rs 4 crore in CSK's purse..IPL 2027 Retention: Wicketless in IPL 2026, Harshal Patel traded from Sunrisers Hyderabad to Gujarat Titans Harshal will represent his fifth IPL franchise, having played 14 seasons in the tournament. He has featured in 124 matches for Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Delhi Capitals, Punjab Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad, taking 151 wickets at an economy rate of 8.92. .IPL 2027 Retention Live Updates: Dhoni's decision remains crucial A final call on Dhoni's playing future will be closely followed by CSK supporters. A consistent performer over the years, the seasoned campaigner was the leading wicket-taker in the 2021 and 2024 editions of the tournament, representing Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) and Punjab Kings (PBKS), respectively..IPL 2027 Retention: CSK already make moves in the trade market Chennai Super Kings have added Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards through trades ahead of the mini-auction. The franchise finished runners-up in the 2026 season and already has a strong core of players. However, not everyone is certain to continue with the team..IPL Retention 2027: No RTM cards make auction bidding more interesting The absence of RTM cards could make the auction more competitive, especially for players who are released by their previous franchises. Teams will have to decide whether to retain a player now or take their chances in the auction..IPL Retention 2027: Can teams keep their entire squad? All you need to know With the IPL 2027 mini-auction approaching, all 10 franchises have the option of keeping their entire existing squad. There is no fixed limit on the number of players a team can retain ahead of the new season. However, every franchise must have between 18 and 25 players in its squad, with overseas players limited to a maximum of eight. Another important point is that teams will not have Right to Match (RTM) cards at the IPL 2027 mini-auction. This means franchises cannot use an RTM option to match another team's winning bid for a released player. They will have to compete through the regular bidding process if they want to bring back their former players.

articles.title: IPL 2027 Retention List: When and where to watch today's announcements; check date, time and live streaming details
articles.summary: The wait is almost over for IPL fans, with all 10 franchises set to submit their list of retained and released players for the 2027 season on Tuesday,
articles.body: The wait is almost over for IPL fans, with all 10 franchises set to submit their list of retained and released players for the 2027 season on Tuesday, November 17.The original deadline was November 15, but the BCCI extended it by two days. The change reportedly came because the earlier date coincided with the fifth and final ODI between India and New Zealand.With several big player trades already completed, the retention announcements are expected to bring more clarity on the squads ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction.IPL 2027 retention list: DeadlineAll 10 franchises must submit their list of retained and released players to the BCCI by Tuesday, November 17, 2026.The teams will reveal which players they want to keep for the next season and which ones they have decided to release. Players released by their franchises will become part of the auction pool.What time will the IPL 2027 retention list be announced?The BCCI and the official broadcaster have not confirmed the exact announcement time. However, reports suggest that the programme will begin at 5:40 PM IST.The announcements are expected to take place in the evening, following the trend from previous seasons.Where to watch IPL 2027 retention list live?Fans can watch the IPL 2027 retention announcements live on the Star Sports Network.The live stream will be available on the JioHotstar app and website in India.What is the IPL retention list?Before every IPL auction, all 10 franchises submit the names of players they want to retain and those they wish to release.Retained players remain with their respective teams for the upcoming season, while released players enter the auction pool and can be picked by any franchise.The rules for retaining players depend on the type of auction. Ahead of a mega auction, franchises have to follow a fixed limit on the number of players they can retain. However, there is no fixed retention limit ahead of a mini-auction.There will be no mega auction before IPL 2027. The teams will instead prepare for a mini-auction, which is scheduled to take place in Goa on December 16, 2026.IPL 2027 Retention: How many players can IPL teams retain?There is no fixed limit on the number of players a franchise can retain ahead of a mini-auction.However, teams must follow the squad-size rules. Each franchise can have a maximum of 25 players, including no more than eight overseas players.What is the IPL 2027 salary cap?The total salary cap for each franchise for IPL 2027 is Rs 157 crore.The amount spent on retained players will be deducted from the total purse. The remaining amount will be available to the franchise at the mini-auction.IPL 2027 mini-auction: Date and venueThe IPL 2027 mini-auction will be held in Goa on December 16, 2026.Since this is a mini-auction, teams will have the opportunity to strengthen their squads by signing players released by other franchises and those who enter the auction pool.IPL 2027 retention list: Key detailsDetailsInformationRetention deadlineTuesday, November 17, 2026Total teams10Auction typeMini-auctionMini-auction dateDecember 16, 2026Mini-auction venueGoaSalary capRs 157 crore per franchiseLive telecastStar Sports NetworkLive streamingJioHotstarIPL 2027: List of confirmed player tradesSeveral high-profile trades have already taken place ahead of the retention deadline. Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings were involved in a major exchange involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh.Rishabh Pant has also returned to Delhi Capitals, while Kuldeep Yadav has moved to Lucknow Super Giants.Sunrisers Hyderabad have been among the busiest teams in the trade market. T Natarajan has returned to the franchise, with Zeeshan Ansari moving to Delhi Capitals.SRH have also brought in Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis from Chennai Super Kings in exchange for Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards.IPL 2027 Retention: List of confirmed player tradesPLAYERPREVIOUS TEAMNEW TEAMHardik PandyaMumbai IndiansPunjab KingsArshdeep SinghPunjab KingsMumbai IndiansRishabh PantLucknow Super GiantsDelhi CapitalsKuldeep YadavDelhi CapitalsLucknow Super GiantsT NatarajanDelhi CapitalsSunrisers HyderabadZeeshan AnsariSunrisers HyderabadDelhi CapitalsLiam LivingstoneSunrisers HyderabadChennai Super KingsJack EdwardsSunrisers HyderabadChennai Super KingsKhaleel AhmedChennai Super KingsSunrisers HyderabadNathan EllisChennai Super KingsSunrisers HyderabadGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: MS Dhoni at CSK: 5 titles, 10 finals and a new role ahead of IPL 2027
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Chennai Super Kings' legendary association with MS Dhoni is entering a new phase.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chennai Super Kings' legendary association with MS Dhoni is entering a new phase. Ahead of IPL 2027, the former captain is set to take up the position of Team Mentor, marking a transition from leading the team on the field to guiding its next generation from the dugout.Since CSK's debut in the inaugural IPL season in 2008, Dhoni has played a central role in shaping the franchise's identity.His leadership brought Chennai five IPL championships and two Champions League T20 titles, while establishing the team as one of the most consistent sides in the competition.By the numbers: Dhoni's CSK legacyAchievementRecordIPL titles as captain5IPL finals10Playoff appearances12 editionsCSK IPL matches as captain221Overall CSK T20 appearances as captain244Matches won145Matches lost96Tied matches1No results2Winning percentage59.42%Champions League T20 trophies2Championship years: 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023.Champions League T20 victories: 2010 and 2014.Five titles and a place among IPL's greatest captainsDhoni's record of five IPL trophies puts him alongside former Mumbai Indians skipper Rohit Sharma for the most championships won by a captain.His achievement in 2010 and 2011 was particularly significant, as he became the first captain to win back-to-back IPL titles.These championship victories helped establish Chennai as a major force in the league and cemented Dhoni's reputation as one of the competition's most successful leaders.Ten finals highlight Chennai's consistency under DhoniCSK's remarkable playoff record stands out as one of the biggest achievements of the Dhoni era. The franchise qualified for the playoffs in 12 editions and reached the final on 10 occasions.Maintaining such a high level of performance over multiple seasons demonstrated the consistency of Dhoni's leadership and the strength of the team he helped build.His overall IPL captaincy numbersDhoni's leadership record extends beyond Chennai Super Kings.Including his 14 matches as captain of Rising Pune Supergiant in 2016, he led teams in 235 IPL matches, securing 136 victories at a win rate of 58.37%.For CSK, his overall T20 captaincy record stands at 244 matches, including Champions League T20 fixtures, with 145 wins, 96 defeats, one tie and two matches ending without a result.Dhoni captained Chennai from 2008 through 2025, with the exception of a brief period in 2022 when Ravindra Jadeja took over the responsibility. He later passed the full-time captaincy to Ruturaj Gaikwad.His appointment as Team Mentor ahead of IPL 2027 represents a new responsibility within the CSK setup. Although his role has evolved, Dhoni's experience and understanding of the game will continue to be an important part of the franchise's plans.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sri Lanka bowled out for 98, created unwanted record as Pakistan pacers run riot in Rawalpindi
articles.summary: Pakistan's fast bowlers dismissed Sri Lanka for 98 on the opening day of the second and series-deciding Test in Rawalpindi on Tuesday, putting the hosts
articles.body: Pakistan's fast bowlers dismissed Sri Lanka for 98 on the opening day of the second and series-deciding Test in Rawalpindi on Tuesday, putting the hosts in a strong position.Mohammad Abbas, Razaullah and Aamer Jamal took three wickets each as Sri Lanka were bowled out in 35.3 overs after Pakistan captain Babar Azam elected to field on a green pitch. Abbas finished with figures of 3-14, Razaullah took 3-21, while Jamal returned 3-24.Skipper Kusal Mendis top-scored with 32, while Sonal Dinusha made 21. They were the only Sri Lankan batters to reach double figures. The total of 98 was lowest at Rawalpindi.Babar had asked his fast bowlers to make use of the conditions after winning the toss, and they delivered. The pitch had grass covering and moisture, allowing the Pakistan pacers to extract seam movement and swing. They maintained their line and length, taking wickets at regular intervals.All 10 Sri Lankan wickets fell to fast bowlers. Razaullah and Abbas struck at regular intervals to put Sri Lanka on the back foot, with Razaullah using his pace to trouble the batters. Jamal then wrapped up the lower order as Pakistan completed the innings with a collective bowling effort.Apart from Mendis and Dinusha, none of the Sri Lankan batters managed to offer much resistance. Pakistan will now look to build on their advantage with a strong batting display.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'We wouldn't play if we weren't confident tournament could be delivered safely': ILT20 Interim COO Michael Fordham
articles.summary: As the ILT20 prepares to enter its fifth season, interim COO Michael Fordham believes the league has established itself among the leading T20 competitions
articles.body: As the ILT20 prepares to enter its fifth season, interim COO Michael Fordham believes the league has established itself among the leading T20 competitions in the world. Having been involved since its inception, Fordham discusses the challenges of organising the new season amid uncertainty in the Middle East, the league's international identity, its emphasis on developing UAE and Associate cricket, and the need to build a sustainable fan base.He also explains how the ILT20 intends to differentiate itself in an increasingly crowded franchise cricket landscape, while outlining its ambitions to expand its reach and strengthen its position in the global game.Excerpts:Q. How have things been in the past couple of months since taking over the interim COO role?Michael Fordham: It's been good. It's been busy. I've been involved in the league since since the outset, since even before Season 1, helping to put it all together and overseeing various aspects. So I familiar with the various workings of ILT20 and all of our internal teams, our stakeholders, franchises, partners, etc.So it hasn't been too much of a learning curve, but obviously it's a slightly different and expanded role. I've been in Dubai for most of that time. It's obviously been a slightly challenging time for the Middle East as a region this year. But we're hopeful that, you know, with just over a week to go, we're going to be in position to deliver a great tournament for ILT20 Season 5.Q. What are your biggest priorities when it comes to starting a new season? When you pitch to prospective players, to prospective teams? What is the pitch for Season 5?Fordham: Heading into the fifth season, the league is reasonably well established now. I think it's one of the top three T20 leagues in the world. So I think we've established ourselves quite well. But obviously, you don't want to rest on your laurels. You've got to continue to grow and continue to expand and continue to make everything a success.So we were keen to, first of all, get as wide a selection of players available for this season as possible. We've moved to a slightly earlier window this year. In previous years, the first three seasons, it was all played in the early part of the year, January, February time. Last year, it started in December and just finished at the beginning of January. And this year, we're at the earliest start yet, starting on the 21st of November. And I think that's a positive. I think it's probably the best window we could have chosen this year for player availability, less clash with other leagues. So a pretty clear window for that.Heading into the fifth season, the league is reasonably well established now. I think it's one of the top three T20 leagues in the world. But obviously, you don't want to rest on your laurels.And we've had quite a big refresh in terms of the squad compositions this year. There were not too many retentions or direct signings that each team was allowed to make after Season 4. So we had a big player auction on the 1st of October. So during the summer, we had a player registration open for that. And the auction was held on the 1st of October, which went very well. All the squads were chosen there. I would say they're pretty well-balanced teams. It's pretty hard to tell which team looks the strongest, which is always a good sign. And we've got a lot of good new players into the league. So I think we've achieved that aim of bringing in some different players.And this is always an attractive league for players to come to. Players like coming to the UAE. They're familiar with it. They love the facilities, the weather, the hotels. They don't have to travel too much during the season, which is a positive compared to a lot of other leagues. I think we've achieved the objective of getting a good group of players in for this year.Now it's two things, really. One is deliver a smooth season operationally. Make sure that everything goes well in the venues and all of the logistics and everything like that. And the other is obviously try and make it as big a commercial and financial success as possible for the league and all of its stakeholders, including the franchises.We've been in touch with the government and the government officials every step of the way regarding their advice, and we wouldn't play this tournament if we weren't confident that it could be delivered safely.Q. Many other sporting events have either been rescheduled or cancelled completely in the region. Considering the challenge that the Middle East poses at this point, how much of a difficulty has it been to convince players, coaches, staff to come into the country?Fordham: To be honest, it hasn't been too much of a challenge convincing players and other partners to come to the UAE. I think players are pretty confident that we will put the right measures in place to ensure their safety. We've been in touch with the government and the government officials every step of the way regarding their advice, and we wouldn't play this tournament if we weren't confident that it could be delivered safely.It's been a tough year for the Middle East as a region, starting from February onwards. But actually in the UAE for the last few months, it's been pretty quiet on that front. And every indication is that we'll be able to launch safely and smoothly.That said, it would be remiss if we didn't have some kind of contingency plans in place. So we have looked at alternate solutions if the situation did escalate. But I think at the moment, everybody is confident that the season can go ahead smoothly.As I'm sure you're aware, the Abu Dhabi T10 is currently taking place just down the road at Abu Dhabi. That has started off very well without incident. So actually, that means quite a few of the players from the ILT20 are already in the UAE. The Abu Dhabi Golf Championships took place last weekend with most of the top golfers from around Europe and around the world taking part. There's another big golf tournament in Dubai this weekend. Those tournaments are going ahead. So actually, I think the outlook for sports in the UAE hopefully is pretty positive right now.Q. What are the contingency plans?Fordham: We have explored other possible venues. There is one in particular that would be considered in the case of things escalating. But as we currently stand, we are 100% full steam ahead for UAE and starting here at Dubai International Stadium next Saturday.Q. What have your learnings been for the past four seasons or even the last season?Fordham: I think the first thing you've got to think about with any sports property, not just cricket, is actually making sure that the sport itself, the action on the field is as good as possible and as competitive as possible. And over the four seasons, I think we've done that well. The fact that we've had four different winners of this tournament in four seasons is pretty exciting and shows that it's a pretty level playing field in the teams in terms of their ability.The on-field product of this event is very strong, not just the players but the match officials, everything like that. We have really good six franchises, some of whom have teams in other leagues, some of whom don't, but they're committed to making this season a success. So cricket-wise, I think we're in great shape, and we'll be the same again this year.Beyond that, we've got to try and make it as big a tournament as possible with its marketing, with its social media presence, with its broadcast presence. We have a fantastic TV partner in India with Zee, who are fully committed to this and showcasing this league through all of their channels. They have a new channel this year (United8 Sports) so that's a bit exciting to see how that goes.And then in terms of our marketing activities as a league, it's a couple of things. We want to make it as big as possible for those who are viewing it around the world, both on broadcast and on digital. So we've invested a lot this year with social media and other content providers in that regard. We've got some new partners coming on board. And then with our promotions in the UAE, obviously that's all about trying to get as many people in the stadium as possible, selling as many tickets as possible, and creating as much buzz as we can in the UAE. And with that in mind, we're trying a few new things this year to try and increase the awareness and increase the buzz throughout the tournament.Q. Coming to the cricket of it all. It's very important for leagues to have a good combination of local players and foreigners. And in ILT20's case, there are quite a few Associate players. So how do you ensure that everything stays in tandem?Fordham: It's quite an interesting squad composition with this league. It's quite a mix of players and one of the things we're very proud about, one of the things I'm very passionate about, is ILT20's role in developing cricket in certain markets and spreading the game globally.First and foremost, that includes the UAE. So in each team, there has to be a minimum of four UAE players in the squad, two of whom have to play at least in the matchday playing eleven. We've seen some fantastic performances from UAE players over the four seasons so far, and I'm sure that will be the same again. The UAE players were very much in demand at the auction.In addition to that, there has to be an Associate player from another nation within the playing eleven. And we've got players all over the cricketing world really being signed up in those associate squads. So USA, Scotland, Namibia, Nepal, all sorts of different places. And that's fantastic to give players from other countries an opportunity.And in addition to that, we're very committed to growing cricket and having our players in the other Gulf countries. So we're very happy to have partnerships with both Kuwait cricket and Saudi Arabian cricket. So there's just a player from each of those nations in every squad. And actually, this year, we're also going to be having some match officials, umpires from those two countries with the match officials team.We're very proud of our role in growing cricket in the region. This year also, we have a high number of Afghanistan players with a partnership with the Afghan board. There's an Irish player in every squad. So it really is a very multicultural, multinational tournament with the players and probably one of the most, probably the most international T20 tournament. And I think that's something that's pretty exciting and unique about this league.Q. Do these mandatory rules restrict the teams, the coaches from picking the ideal playing XI?Fordham: Not really. We've got two UAE players and another associate in the match XI. So there's another eight players that can come from any of the Full Member or other Associate countries. So that's a pretty wide selection of talent available. And I think you've seen that with the players signed up for the auction.You've got pretty much every Test nation and many Associate nations represented in our squads. It's a real mix of experienced T20 superstars and some younger upcoming players. We've got people like Thomas Rew, who's playing for the first time this year. He was one of the top young players from England. Him playing alongside, and against legends of the game who've been around for a long time, like a Faf du Plessis or Andre Russell's. It's something that makes this a really compelling tournament. So I think that the franchises sort of lean into that and enjoy the strategy around building a team from different nationalities and different skill sets. So yeah, there are not too many issues there. I think it's something that people like about this league.Q. When it comes to growing a league, India and UAE are important markets. But how do you go over and above that?Fordham: You're right that those probably are the two key markets. India, clearly, due to its massive passion for cricket and size of the commercial market and geographic and time zone proximity to the UAE, is obviously vital.The UAE is our home market. Clearly any sports competition needs to have its local fan base. So it is key that we promote and produce coverage into the UAE and the wider Middle East. That's vital.But as I said, this is an incredibly international tournament with players from all over the world. So we have to have broadcast coverage and digital coverage in every cricketing nation, from Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, UK, Australia, South Africa, the Caribbean, the USA. These are all key markets for us. And all of our partners play a role in that. Broadcasters, other media partners, and our sponsors all play a role in promoting into those places.Q. When it comes to the T20 leagues, there is significant competition among all of them for getting the best talent, the best sponsors, the broadcasters. How do you envision ILT20 standing out?Fordham: A few things really. As you say, it is a crowded schedule for T20 leagues. Every country in the cricket world pretty much has a T20 league now or a T10 league So I think we stand out with quite a few things.One is the franchises. We have a real great mix of franchises. Three who have brand IPL and three who don't. That's quite a mix rather than being a league that is all IPL teams like maybe the SA20.The international nature of this tournament from its playing base, probably more players from more different nationalities than any other tournament makes this one stand out and feel quite compelling.The UAE as a destination itself is a huge multicultural hotspot and a melting pot of people from all over the world. And I think that's reflected in the event. But yeah, this being a place that people love to come, whether that's fans and tourists on holiday because of the weather at this time of year, players love coming here.So I think we've sort of created quite a kind of niche for ourselves and a very appealing tournament for players to come in. They get well looked after. They enjoy bringing their families out to Dubai. It's a great place to be at any time of year, especially this time of year when the cricket is on. So hopefully some of those are the factors that mean that we can stand out in a crowded market.Q. What about the players in such a scenario? Some players don't play the entire season and jump to another T20 league. How can that issue be addressed?Fordham: Yeah, it's a good question. And you hit on one of the central challenges of global cricket, not just faced by this league. But as I said right at the start of this, the most important thing about any sports competition is the on-field product.By that, I mean the competitiveness and crucially, players trying their hardest and bona fide competition between the players, between the teams. And I really feel like we have that in this tournament.I remember talking to some of the umpires last season, and they said that they felt this was as competitive tournament as any in the world. And I definitely feel that.The players seem to care for the teams that they play for. A team like the Desert Vipers or a Gulf Giants who aren't in other leagues in the world, they've built that sort of culture of wanting to play for the team and, built that team identity and team culture through the owners and the management.It definitely feels that this isn't just a case of them (players) turning up at another tournament and not really caring what happens. This is a bona fide competitive league where the on-field actions take precedence.Q. What is the long-term vision for the ILT20? Where do you see it going and what can be expected from the ILT20?Fordham: The long-term vision is simply to carry on what we're doing, but continue to grow each year and do new things. You know, grow our audience, grow our viewership, grow our attendances in stadium, grow commercial revenues, become even more established as one of the top T20 leagues in the world. I think we can grow more across the Middle East.Our partnerships with Kuwait and Saudi Arabia are really exciting. I think this is a real region which has got a lot of potential for cricket. Actually, a lot of talent on the field coming through, but actually a lot of fans that we can engage better with and do more with. So it's just more of the same, really.Growing, providing entertainment for everybody, and, you know, being a well-run, well-respected league. Continuing in that regard would be the long-term objective.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'He discredited the man himself': Ashwin tears into Pat Cummins over Usman Khawaja, makes big Sandpaper-gate claim
articles.summary: Former India spinner R Ashwin has expressed surprise at the manner in which Australia captain Pat Cummins responded to Usman Khawaja's claims about the
articles.body: Former India spinner R Ashwin has expressed surprise at the manner in which Australia captain Pat Cummins responded to Usman Khawaja's claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, suggesting that the controversy continues to divide the Australian dressing room even eight years later.In his autobiography, 'Sabr: Finding My Way in Cricket and Life', Khawaja alleged that the entire Australian team knew about the ball-tampering plan. This contradicted the findings of Cricket Australia's investigation, which held only three players, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, responsible.Cummins strongly rejected the claims, describing them as "100% wrong" and "complete and utter nonsense". He also denied knowing that sandpaper had been brought onto the field.Ashwin, however, was taken aback by the Australian captain's response, arguing that he had questioned Khawaja's credibility rather than simply challenging his account."Firstly, when Usman Khawaja has mentioned certain things in his book, those are his accounts of the story and we need to respect that. But what happened at Pat Cummins's press conference is that he didn't discredit Usman Khawaja's account of the story; he discredited the man himself. And that is the problem for me," Ashwin said on JioStar."When you can't discredit someone's information, you discredit the person. I know Usman Khawaja; I've played a lot of cricket with him, not on a personal front. He is a man of high integrity and really honest and up-and-straightforward person."The former India off-spinner also pointed out that Cummins, who was on his third tour at the time of the 2018 scandal, was unlikely to have been part of the leadership group. Ashwin believed that group comprised Smith, Warner and possibly Tim Paine."I genuinely thought that this conversation would have centred around saying, 'I wasn't aware of what exactly was happening. I wasn't a part of the leadership group.' It was very surprising for me that Pat Cummins had to come to the press conference and discredit the person himself. That was a little bit of a shock to me, watching from afar," he added.The scandal erupted during the third Test against South Africa at Newlands in March 2018, when Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper on the ball. Smith, Warner and Bancroft were subsequently banned by Cricket Australia.While Ashwin praised Cummins for helping lead Australian cricket's transition alongside Tim Paine after the controversy, he felt recent comments from the captain and Warner indicated that differences over the episode remained."Pat Cummins, who I really admire as a cricketer, is the captain of Australia and, alongside Tim Paine, took on the new regime of trying to rebrand Australian cricket after that incident. He has come out and called what Khawaja has said baseless, nonsense, and something that does not have proof," Ashwin said."David Warner has continued on his own thread of saying what he believes is right. So one thing is crystal clear: there were cracks in that Australian dressing room in terms of views and opinions on this, and I don't think it is crackless even now."Ashwin also referred to former Australia pacer Chadd Sayers, who backed Khawaja's claims. Sayers said the entire team knew about the plan and recalled removing sandpaper from the field as the 12th man during the Port Elizabeth Test, which preceded the Cape Town match.The 40-year-old believes these accounts support Khawaja's call for collective accountability rather than placing responsibility solely on the three players who were punished."What's happened at the end of this book being written is that Usman Khawaja, while he has said all those statements and given his story, has made only one thing very clear, which is: he is asking for collective accountability. He is saying, which is pretty accurate in this case, that it was not only three people who knew about it; there were more," Ashwin said."And with what we saw of Chadd Sayers and what Usman Khawaja is saying, that makes it five already. So he is right."Hayden, Irfan Pathan also seek answersFormer Australia opener Matthew Hayden said supporters deserved clarity, arguing that the fresh accounts had reopened questions about trust and accountability."The fundamental question here is: what was damaged, and why is it relevant? And it's as simple as this: it's because when integrity is broken, trust then gets damaged, and all of these new accounts have just reopened the questions of accountability. So supporters, in my opinion, really deserve clear answers," he said."Eight years passing doesn't automatically resolve the hurt or the disagreement..."Former India pacer Irfan Pathan also questioned whether bowlers could have remained unaware of any deliberate alteration to the ball, particularly when reverse swing was involved."It's not possible that, if the ball is reverse swinging and as a bowler, I won't know if something has been done to the ball. I'll know straight away..."Pathan added that the matter should be investigated again if Australian media and supporters continued to seek answers."If something has happened, and if Australian media and people want answers, then the investigation should start again."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Simplicity': Ruturaj Gaikwad reveals the biggest lesson MS Dhoni taught him at CSK
articles.summary: Chennai Super Kings (CSK) skipper Ruturaj Gaikwad has paid an emotional tribute to MS Dhoni following the announcement that the former India captain will
articles.body: Chennai Super Kings (CSK) skipper Ruturaj Gaikwad has paid an emotional tribute to MS Dhoni following the announcement that the former India captain will move into a new role as the franchise's Team Mentor ahead of the IPL 2027 season. Reflecting on his time alongside the legendary cricketer, Gaikwad highlighted the invaluable lessons he picked up from Dhoni and thanked him for the opportunity to share the dressing room and the field.Dhoni, who has spent 17 seasons with CSK, will now step away from his playing career in the Indian Premier League, bringing an end to an association that has been central to the tournament since its inaugural edition in 2008. The 45-year-old, one of the most recognisable faces in the competition, will continue to remain connected with the five-time champions in a mentoring capacity.Gaikwad, who succeeded Dhoni as CSK captain before the 2024 season, took to Instagram to share his thoughts on the former skipper. Recalling his arrival at the franchise in 2019, the current CSK captain said the biggest takeaway from observing Dhoni was his simplicity, despite the extraordinary success he had achieved throughout his career.“Simplicity,” wrote Gaikwad in his Instagram post, before adding, "I got to learn the exact meaning of this word when I first joined CSK in 2019 by watching you through the lens as much as possible, that was the biggest lesson I learned despite of all the achievements that you have accumulated over the years! To share the dressing room ,the field,the 22 yards and to finish games with you is what are dreams made of. You are and You Will always Be OUR THAALAA, our captain and our Leader! Thank you Mahi bhai for everything."While his playing days in the IPL have come to an end, Dhoni's influence within the CSK setup is set to continue. His new assignment will see him draw on years of experience to mentor players, contribute to the franchise's planning and help shape its future generation of cricketers.Dhoni's association with Chennai has been marked by remarkable consistency and an enviable trophy haul. Under his leadership, CSK established themselves as one of the most successful teams in the competition, winning five IPL titles. The franchise also captured the Champions League T20 crown in 2010 and 2014, adding to its achievements in franchise cricket.CSK's success under Dhoni was built around a distinct team culture that prioritised stability, trust and composure in high-pressure situations. His approach to leadership, particularly his faith in experienced players and ability to extract the best from individuals, became a defining feature of the franchise. Chennai regularly featured in the playoffs and finals, with Dhoni's calm presence playing a major role in the team's sustained success.His IPL journey, however, was not limited entirely to CSK. During the franchise's two-year suspension, Dhoni turned out for Rising Pune Supergiant in the 2016 and 2017 seasons. He returned to Chennai in 2018 and made an immediate impact, leading the team to the IPL title in his comeback season.The transition in leadership at CSK began ahead of the 2024 campaign, when Dhoni handed over the captaincy to Gaikwad. He nevertheless continued as a player, offering his inputs behind the stumps while also contributing with the bat in crucial moments towards the end of innings.Dhoni's last appearance in the IPL came against Gujarat Titans during the 2025 season. A calf injury subsequently ruled him out of the entire 2026 edition.In a career spanning 278 IPL matches, Dhoni accumulated 5,439 runs at an average of 38.30 and a strike rate of 137.45. His record includes 24 half-centuries and 264 sixes, underlining his reputation as one of the most effective middle-order batters and finishers in the tournament's history.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: The IPL franchises will confirm their retained and released players on November 17, 2026. The retention announcements are crucial for teams ahead of the mini...
articles.body:
The wait is almost over for IPL fans, with all 10 franchises set to submit their list of retained and released players for the 2027 season on Tuesday, November 17. The original deadline was November 15, but the BCCI extended it by two days. The change reportedly came because the earlier date coincided with the fifth and final ODI between India and New Zealand. With several big player trades already completed, the retention announcements are expected to bring more clarity on the squads ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction.

All 10 franchises must submit their list of retained and released players to the BCCI by Tuesday, November 17, 2026. The teams will reveal which players they want to keep for the next season and which ones they have decided to release. Players released by their franchises will become part of the auction pool.

What time will the IPL 2027 retention list be announced?

The BCCI and the official broadcaster have not confirmed the exact announcement time. However, reports suggest that the programme will begin at 5:40 PM IST. The announcements are expected to take place in the evening, following the trend from previous seasons.

Where to watch IPL 2027 retention list live?

Fans can watch the IPL 2027 retention announcements live on the Star Sports Network. The live stream will be available on the JioHotstar app and website in India.

Before every IPL auction, all 10 franchises submit the names of players they want to retain and those they wish to release. Retained players remain with their respective teams for the upcoming season, while released players enter the auction pool and can be picked by any franchise. The rules for retaining players depend on the type of auction. Ahead of a mega auction, franchises have to follow a fixed limit on the number of players they can retain. However, there is no fixed retention limit ahead of a mini-auction. There will be no mega auction before IPL 2027. The teams will instead prepare for a mini-auction, which is scheduled to take place in Goa on December 16, 2026.

IPL 2027 Retention: How many players can IPL teams retain?

There is no fixed limit on the number of players a franchise can retain ahead of a mini-auction. However, teams must follow the squad-size rules. Each franchise can have a maximum of 25 players, including no more than eight overseas players.

The total salary cap for each franchise for IPL 2027 is Rs 157 crore. The amount spent on retained players will be deducted from the total purse. The remaining amount will be available to the franchise at the mini-auction.

The IPL 2027 mini-auction will be held in Goa on December 16, 2026. Since this is a mini-auction, teams will have the opportunity to strengthen their squads by signing players released by other franchises and those who enter the auction pool.

Rishabh Pant has also returned to Delhi Capitals, while Kuldeep Yadav has moved to Lucknow Super Giants. Sunrisers Hyderabad have been among the busiest teams in the trade market. T Natarajan has returned to the franchise, with Zeeshan Ansari moving to Delhi Capitals.
